concepts.learning_objective: Define a tissue and recall that complex animals have only four basic tissue types.
Explain how tissues form organs and organs form organ systems, showing division of labour.
Distinguish morphology (external form) from anatomy (internal organs) in animals.
Identify the class, phylum and common Indian species of frog.
Explain why frogs are called cold-blooded or poikilotherms.
Describe camouflage, aestivation and hibernation as adaptations of frogs.
Describe the moist, mucus-covered skin of the frog and its role in water uptake.
Identify the external features of the frog's head, trunk and limbs.
Distinguish male and female frogs by vocal sacs and copulatory pads.

topics.title: Digestive and respiratory systems of frog

concepts.learning_objective: Trace the parts of the frog's alimentary canal and relate its length to diet.
Explain the roles of HCl, gastric juice, bile and pancreatic juice in digestion.
Compare cutaneous and pulmonary respiration in the frog.

topics.title: Circulatory and excretory systems of frog

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the frog's three-chambered heart, closed circulation and portal systems.
Distinguish blood from lymph and recall that frog RBCs are nucleated.
Describe the frog's excretory organs and explain why it is ureotelic.
Classify parts of the frog's nervous system into central, peripheral and autonomic divisions.
Identify the parts of the fore-brain, mid-brain and hind-brain of the frog.
Identify the frog's sense organs and distinguish well-organised ones from cellular aggregations.

topics.title: Reproduction in frog and its importance

concepts.learning_objective: Trace the path of sperms through the male reproductive system of the frog.
Describe the female reproductive system, external fertilisation and tadpole development.
Explain the ecological and economic importance of frogs.
